title: Ladder of Nice
intro: Nice, good, bad — the three words that do all the work and none of the precision. Climb the ladder to the word that actually fits.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'good' about food
A2.why: Only for food and drink: a delicious paella, not a delicious film.

A2.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about a person who gives a lot
A2.why: Generous people share their time, money or food.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'bad' about weather or a situation
A2.why: “Awful weather” is much stronger than “bad weather”.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'nice' about how something looks
A2.why: For things you see: a beautiful beach, a beautiful dress.

A2.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about someone's personality
A2.why: A friendly person is easy to talk to and smiles a lot.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'bad' about food or a smell that makes you feel sick
A2.why: Very strong: the food or smell makes you feel sick.

A2.right: a more precise way to say 'good' at doing something
A2.why: A talented guitarist has a natural gift.

A2.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about a place to sit or sleep
A2.why: Say it in three parts: COMF-ta-ble.

A2.right: a stronger way to say 'good' about a holiday or a film
A2.why: Enthusiastic and positive: “The holiday was fantastic!”

A2.right: a more precise way to say 'bad' about someone's manners
A2.why: A rude waiter doesn't say please or thank you.

A2.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about a room where everything is in its place
A2.why: A tidy room is ordered, nothing on the floor.

A2.right: a more precise way to say 'bad' about a road or place that could hurt you
A2.why: Precise: the problem is the risk, not just “bad”.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about an experience
B1.why: A pleasant evening: calm, nice, nothing special.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about someone who thinks of others
B1.why: Considerate people think about others: they phone if they'll be late.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'bad' — very strong, almost shocking
a more precise way to say 'nice' about someone's appearance
a more precise way to say 'good' — exceptionally so
B1.why: It “stands out” from all the others.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'bad' — mild, about something you didn't enjoy
B1.why: Mild and polite: an unpleasant smell, an unpleasant trip.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about someone's manner
B1.why: A charming person makes you feel good with their manners.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'good' about someone you can always count on
B1.why: A reliable mechanic does the job well, every time.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'nice' about a flat with lots of room
B1.why: From “space”: plenty of room to move.

B1.right: a more precise way to say 'good' about how someone uses their hands or tools
a more precise way to say 'bad' about something that damages your health
a more precise way to say 'good' about food that makes you hungry just looking at it
B1.why: Your mouth “waters” when you see it: “una pinta que se te hace la boca agua”.

B2.right: an even stronger, more vivid 'nice' — genuinely pleasing, full of charm
B2.why: A delightful afternoon or person gives real pleasure.

B2.right: an even stronger 'bad' — cruel, shocking treatment of people or animals
an even stronger 'nice' — delicate and finely made, like lace or a fine dish
B2.why: For fine detail and quality: exquisite embroidery, exquisite cooking.

B2.right: an even more precise 'bad' — a day or journey that is exhausting and hard
B2.why: British spelling with -ll: a gruelling climb, a gruelling twelve-hour shift.

B2.right: an even more precise 'nice' — welcoming to guests
B2.why: Same family as “hospitality”: making guests feel at home.

B2.right: an even more precise 'good' — extremely careful with detail
B2.why: A meticulous doctor checks everything twice.

B2.right: an even stronger 'bad' — so low in quality or standard it seems to have no bottom
B2.why: From “abyss”: so low you can't see the bottom.

B2.right: an even stronger 'nice' — a story or speaker that holds your attention completely
B2.why: It “captures” you: you can't look away.

B2.right: an even stronger 'good' — so useful you can't put a price on it
B2.why: Spanish trap: invaluable = extremely valuable, not worthless.

B2.right: an even stronger 'bad' — dirty, miserable living conditions
B2.why: Victorian slums were squalid: dirty and neglected.

B2.right: an even more precise 'good' — finding clever solutions with very little
B2.why: A resourceful cowboy fixes his wagon with rope and a stick.

B2.right: an even stronger 'nice' — a view so beautiful it amazes you
B2.why: It “takes your breath away”: the view from the Sierra Calderona.

C1.right: the most elevated 'nice' — a beauty beyond ordinary description
C1.why: Used for art, music or nature that seems almost spiritual.

C1.right: the strongest 'bad' — a situation that is extremely serious or urgent
C1.why: Collocations: dire consequences, in dire need, the situation is dire.

C1.right: the strongest 'good' — flawless, without a single fault
C1.why: Impeccable manners, impeccable English: nothing to correct.

C1.right: the strongest 'bad' — behaviour you must condemn morally
C1.why: From “reprehend”, to criticise: a moral judgement.

C1.right: the strongest 'nice' — generous and forgiving on a grand scale
C1.why: Latin “great soul”: generous even to a defeated rival.

C1.right: the strongest 'good' — a model that others should follow
C1.why: From “example”: exemplary conduct deserves to be copied.

C1.right: the strongest 'bad' — an error so obvious it stands out from the rest
C1.why: Latin “out of the herd”: it stands out, for the wrong reasons.

C1.right: a refined 'nice' — friendly, warm and sociable in atmosphere
C1.why: A convivial dinner: good food, good company, lots of talk.

C1.right: a refined 'nice' — a healthy, respectable area to live in
C1.why: Often used negatively and with humour: “not a very salubrious area”.

C1.right: a formal, precise 'good' — a remedy or treatment that works
C1.why: It simply means “effective”: an efficacious treatment works.

C1.right: the strongest 'bad' — harmful in a slow, hidden way
C1.why: Pernicious effects grow quietly over time.

C1.right: the strongest 'good' — a musician's dazzling skill
C1.why: A virtuoso performance: technical brilliance, like a great guitarist.
